requirement_title: Feature Request: Allow generation of Formatter for a type in a referenced assembly
requirement_text:
# REQ-2129: Feature Request: Allow generation of Formatter for a type in a referenced assembly

Source: https://github.com/MessagePack-CSharp/MessagePack-CSharp/issues/2129
Type: feature

## Requirement

Given Project A (contains `ProjectA.MyType`, has no and cannot have a reference to the MessagePack NuGet package) and Project B (references Project A and MessagePack), the reporter needs a source-generated `IMessagePackFormatter` for `ProjectA.MyType` generated inside Project B.

Proposed solution: add a `[GeneratedMessagePackFormatter]` attribute that works for partial classes implementing `IMessagePackFormatter<T>`:

```csharp
[GeneratedMessagePackFormatter]
partial class MyObjectFormatter: IMessagePackFormatter<MyObject>;
```

The class does not need a body; the implementation is source-generated by `MessagePack.SourceGenerator.MessagePackGenerator` as usual.

For attribute-based property keys and other settings (such as Union), the issue lists three alternatives: (1) use `System.Runtime.Serialization.DataMember` and related attributes; (2) let the generator and analyzers work with user-defined copies of the MessagePack attributes; (3) source-generate the attributes themselves via `RegisterPostInitializationOutput`.

Motivation: Project A is a NuGet library that should stay minimal with zero dependencies.

## Acceptance criteria

- A `[GeneratedMessagePackFormatter]` attribute exists and can be applied to a partial class implementing `IMessagePackFormatter<T>`.
- The source generator emits the formatter implementation for `T` inside the annotated class, in the assembly that declares the class (Project B), even when `T` is declared in a referenced assembly.
- The annotated class may be declared without a body (`partial class X : IMessagePackFormatter<T>;`).
- `T` needs no MessagePack attributes: without `[DataContract]` or `[MessagePackObject]` on `T` the generated formatter uses contractless behaviour over public members. (derived from maintainer comment)
- If `T` does carry MessagePack attributes, they are honoured. (derived from maintainer comment)
- Private members are not required to be serialized; only public members are in scope. (derived from maintainer comment)
- Project A needs no reference to the MessagePack package. (derived)

## Notes from discussion

- AArnott: "We might simplistically say this only works in 'contractless' mode, such that you need no attributes on it at all. If there are attributes on it, fine, we'll use them. But if there is no `[DataContract]` or `[MessagePackObject]` attribute on the type, go contractless by default."
- AArnott on prerequisite: "Does ProjectA.MyType requires only `public` members to be serialized? That seems a prerequisite for anything here." Reporter: yes.
- AArnott is not a fan of a `PropertyKeys` dictionary on the formatter, and warns that copying attributes into Project A breaks reflection-based (dynamic resolver) mode.
- AArnott suggested a surrogate-type design: `[GeneratedMessagePackFormatter(SurrogateType = typeof(ProjectASurrogate))]`, keys mapped by property name; reporter: "Looks good." No design was settled in the thread.

findings.claim: The acceptance criterion that MessagePack attributes on T are honoured is not implemented. The collector never examines T's attributes and unconditionally builds string-keyed contractless members whenever no surrogate is supplied, so a referenced [MessagePackObject] type with integer [Key] members is serialized using its member names instead of its declared keys; DataContract/DataMember settings are likewise not consulted.

receipt_plan.detail: Compile ProjectA.MyObject in a metadata assembly with [MessagePackObject] and [Key(0)], then generate a body-less formatter for it as in GeneratedFormatterRequirementTests.Formatter_MessagePackAttributesOnReferencedType_AreHonored. The generated formatter currently calls WriteMapHeader rather than WriteArrayHeader, proving that the declared integer key is ignored.

findings.claim: Contractless field selection has the read-only test reversed: public mutable instance fields fail IsPublicReadWrite and are silently omitted, while public readonly fields pass and are subsequently modelled as writable. This violates the documented public read-write field behaviour; serialization loses mutable field values, and a type with a selected readonly field can produce invalid deserialization code.

receipt_plan.detail: Run GeneratedFormatterRequirementTests.BodylessFormatter_ReferencedType_UsesPublicReadWriteMembersContractlessly. Its referenced target has a public mutable Volume field and a read-write Label property; the current generated formatter contains Label but no .Volume access. A companion mutation changing IsReadOnly to !IsReadOnly should make that assertion pass.

findings.claim: The public-field eligibility check is inverted: `public int Value;` is excluded from contractless and surrogate generation, while `public readonly int ReadOnly;` is included and then modelled as writable. Consequently mutable public fields silently lose their serialized data, and readonly fields can make the generated formatter fail compilation with an assignment-to-readonly-field error.

receipt_plan.detail: Run Receipts.GeneratedTests.GeneratedFormatterCollectorReceiptTests.ContractlessGeneration_IncludesMutableFieldsAndSkipsReadOnlyFields. It generates a formatter for a type containing both a public mutable field and a public readonly field, requires successful compilation, and checks that only the mutable field appears in the formatter.

findings.claim: When SurrogateType is null, the collector unconditionally builds contractless string-key members and never examines attributes on T. For a referenced type marked [MessagePackObject] whose Value property has [Key(0)] and whose Ignored property has [IgnoreMember], the generated formatter uses string-key map serialization and includes Ignored instead of honouring the declared integer-key array contract. This violates the requirement that MessagePack attributes on T be honoured.

receipt_plan.detail: Run Receipts.GeneratedTests.GeneratedFormatterCollectorReceiptTests.MessagePackAttributesOnReferencedType_AreHonoured. It compiles ProjectA with [MessagePackObject], [Key(0)], and [IgnoreMember], references its metadata from ProjectB, generates the annotated formatter, and requires WriteArrayHeader and omission of Ignored.

hunches.claim: MessagePack attributes on the formatted type are never inspected: whenever SurrogateType is null, the collector unconditionally builds an ordinal-name, string-key contractless model. Consequently, a [MessagePackObject] type with integer [Key] annotations gets a different string-key map instead of the required attributed wire format.

receipt_plan.detail: Add a generator execution test for an external type declared as [MessagePackObject] public class Payload { [Key(0)] public int Value { get; set; } } and a [GeneratedMessagePackFormatter] partial formatter without SurrogateType. Generate its formatter and serialize Payload { Value = 42 }; assert the output is the integer-key array representation required by [Key(0)], rather than a map containing the string "Value". The current implementation produces the map.

hunches.claim: The public-member predicate is inverted for fields: it accepts only public readonly fields and rejects ordinary public mutable fields. Mutable fields are silently omitted from the generated contract, while readonly fields can be selected despite not being writable.

receipt_plan.detail: Generate a formatter for an external class with `public int Mutable;` and serialize an instance with Mutable = 42. Assert that the generated string-key map contains "Mutable" and that deserialization restores it. The current filter excludes this field; also compile a case containing `public readonly int ReadOnly;` to expose the opposite, invalid selection.

hunches.claim: MessagePack attributes on the formatted type are ignored. Collection always chooses contractless members unless a surrogate is supplied, so a type carrying [MessagePackObject] and integer [Key] annotations still receives name-based string keys, contrary to the acceptance criterion that those attributes be honoured.

receipt_plan.detail: Add a generated-formatter execution test for a type declared with [MessagePackObject], a member [Key(0)], and another member [IgnoreMember], without setting SurrogateType. Serialize it and assert the existing MessagePack integer-key array contract and ignored membership; the current collector instead produces contractless string keys.

hunches.claim: Contractless field selection is inverted: public mutable fields are excluded while public readonly fields are included and marked readable/writable. Consequently ordinary public fields are not serialized, and a readonly field can make generated deserialization invalid by assigning to it.

receipt_plan.detail: Add an external class with a public mutable field and a public readonly field, generate its contractless formatter, and round-trip the mutable field. The test should also require successful compilation of the generated formatter; the current field predicate fails these expectations.

hunches.claim: No test exercises public fields, so the field accessibility predicate can exclude every writable public field (and include readonly fields) without any test failing. All external-type fixtures contain only properties.

receipt_plan.detail: src/MessagePack.SourceGenerator/CodeAnalysis/GeneratedFormatterCollector.cs:275 swap-boolean: field.DeclaredAccessibility == Accessibility.Public && field.IsReadOnly && !field.IsConst -> field.DeclaredAccessibility == Accessibility.Public && !field.IsReadOnly && !field.IsConst; expected to survive because every contractless and surrogate execution fixture uses properties rather than fields. Add an external class or struct with a writable public field and a readonly public field and assert that only the writable field round-trips.

hunches.claim: The acceptance criterion that MessagePack attributes on T are honoured has no test. Every execution fixture formats an attribute-free external type, and every generator test uses an unannotated MyType, so a formatter that always applies contractless string keys would pass the suite.

receipt_plan.detail: Add an execution test for a [GeneratedMessagePackFormatter] whose T is [MessagePackObject] with reordered integer [Key] values and an [IgnoreMember] member. Serialize with the generated resolver and assert the integer-key array layout, values, and omission of the ignored member; the current tests would not detect contractless output ignoring those annotations.

hunches.claim: The explicitly supported bodyless declaration form is untested: every attributed formatter in both test projects has a brace-delimited body. Generation or compilation regressions specific to a semicolon-bodied partial class would go unnoticed.

receipt_plan.detail: Add a generator compilation/execution fixture declared as `[GeneratedMessagePackFormatter] public partial class MyFormatter : IMessagePackFormatter<MyType>;`, with no hand-written members, and verify compilation plus a serialize/deserialize round-trip through the generated resolver.

hunches.claim: suppressed by unconfirmed context entry: [L11] area=analyzer, generator: Types that come from a referenced assembly are deliberately not analysed and get no formatter from the compiling assembly. In `TypeCollector.CollectCore`, after the custom-formatter, enum and generic checks, a non-generic type whose symbol is metadata-only exits with a bare `if (type.Locations[0].IsInMetadata) { return; }` (TypeCollector.cs:367-370), so no MsgPack003/004/005 diagnostic and no generated formatter appear for it. The defining assembly owns validating and formatting its own types (rationale inferred: the code has no comment). A missing diagnostic or formatter for such a type is not a defect. (source: src/MessagePack.SourceGenerator/CodeAnalysis/TypeCollector.cs:367) (would-be finding: The existing policy against implicitly analyzing or generating formatters for metadata-only types remains deliberate; this feature is a separate explicit opt-in through [GeneratedMessagePackFormatter], so the new path is consistent with that policy.)

receipt_plan.detail: [L11] records that referenced-assembly types ordinarily receive no analysis or formatter from the compiling assembly. The new attribute-driven request is explicitly declared in the consuming assembly and therefore does not change that default behaviour.

interpretations.label: A
interpretations.summary: Implement the formatter-generation feature together with the suggested optional SurrogateType property, using a Project-B-accessible surrogate type to supply property keys and other settings mapped to T's properties by name. Code: In addition to the core generation, the attribute exposes SurrogateType, the generator resolves and validates that type and maps its attributed properties to T by name, and the resulting metadata controls keys/settings instead of relying solely on T's own attributes or contractless defaults.

interpretations.label: B
interpretations.summary: Add a parameterless GeneratedMessagePackFormatter attribute whose annotated, possibly bodyless partial formatter class receives a generated implementation for T, using public-member contractless serialization by default and honoring any MessagePack attributes already present on T. Code: The generator and any associated declaration-syntax handling need only discover the marker attribute and IMessagePackFormatter<T>, emit Serialize/Deserialize members into that partial class, and inspect T across assembly boundaries; no surrogate-type property or name-based key mapping is implemented.
